evaluations.rationale: Create game is present and complementary game lifecycle stories (invite, start, delete, browse, export) exist in the backlog.
Invite-by-URL has complementary join story (PP-029) and game creation (PP-001) to enable the flow.
Starting a round by entering an item is supported by item add/edit/delete/browse stories (PP-006, PP-007, PP-008, PP-004).
Viewing all items is supported alongside add/edit/delete (PP-006, PP-007, PP-008), so no missing complementary capability.
Selecting an item to be estimated is covered together with item management stories (PP-006..PP-008) and list viewing (PP-004).
Adding items is paired with edit/list/delete stories (PP-007, PP-004, PP-008), so required complementary capabilities exist.
Edit item is complemented by add and delete (PP-006, PP-008) and listing (PP-004); no missing complementary requirement evident.
Delete item is supported within CRUD for items (PP-006 add, PP-007 edit) so no missing complementary capability.
Showing all estimates immediately is supported by estimate collection and reveal stories (PP-032, PP-033) and no complementary story is absent.
Accepting the average of estimates is an end-state action and is supported by estimate capture stories; no missing complementary capability is evident.
Auto-filling estimate when all estimates match relies on estimate visibility and capture (PP-032, PP-033) which are present.
Entering the agreed-upon estimate complements acceptance and round flow (PP-010, PP-003); no necessary capability is missing.
Re-estimating a previously estimated story is supported by storage of prior rounds and browsing (PP-039, PP-016, PP-017).
Importing stories from a spreadsheet is self-contained and has complementary copy/paste option (PP-015) and item add (PP-006); no missing capability.
Copy/paste stories is an alternative import mechanism; supported alongside import (PP-014) and item management (PP-006).
Browsing previous games is supported by storage and transcript viewing/export stories (PP-017, PP-018, PP-019).
Viewing a game transcript is available and complemented by export and browse stories (PP-016, PP-018, PP-019).
Export as HTML is backed by transcript viewing (PP-017); complementary capabilities to produce and access transcripts are present.
Export as CSV is supported by transcript and storage stories (PP-017, PP-016); no missing export-enabling capabilities evident.
Deleting a game is present and balanced by create (PP-001), browse (PP-016), and transcript/export (PP-017..PP-019) stories.
Account creation is present and complemented by login, change, delete, and password reminder stories (PP-022, PP-023, PP-024, PP-026).
Login is supported by account creation (PP-021) and password reminder (PP-026); no missing complementary capability is evident.
Changing account details is present and complements create/delete/login stories (PP-021, PP-022, PP-024); overall account lifecycle is covered.
Account deletion exists and is matched by account creation and management stories (PP-021, PP-023); no missing complementary capability evident.
Timezone display requires timestamps, which are implied by game/transcript storage (PP-017); no complementary capability is noticeably absent.
Password reminder by email complements account creation/login stories (PP-021, PP-022); required supporting capabilities are present conceptually in backlog.
Selecting card sets is self-contained and not missing complementary requirements to be implementable.
Estimator limit is a simple constraint on invites/joins (PP-002, PP-029); complementary capabilities to enforce the limit exist in invite/join flow.
Joining by entering a name complements invite and game creation stories (PP-002, PP-001); necessary complementary capabilities exist.
Seeing the item being estimated is supported by round start/selection and item listing (PP-003, PP-005, PP-004).
Seeing all items for the session is covered by item list and storage stories (PP-004, PP-006); no missing complementary requirement.
Immediate visibility that an estimator has played is supported by capture and reveal stories (PP-033, PP-036); required capabilities are present.
Showing all estimates when all have played is paired with estimation and reveal mechanics (PP-032, PP-034); complementary parts present.
Allowing estimate changes until last selection is consistent with other estimate-capture and reveal stories (PP-033, PP-041); no missing complementary capability.
Showing prior estimates requires storing historical estimates; prior-round browsing/export stories (PP-039, PP-016, PP-017) exist to support this.
Seeing who gave what during current round is supported by estimate capture and participant identification stories (PP-032, PP-029); no complementary capability missing.
Starting a shared two-minute timer is self-contained and complemented by reset behavior (PP-038); no missing complementary capability identified.
Automatic timer reset after all play relies on estimate capture (PP-033) and timer start (PP-037); complementary capabilities exist.
Scrolling back through prior rounds is supported by transcript/browse/export stories (PP-017, PP-016); storage required is present elsewhere in backlog.
Maintaining card order across draws is an internal UI/UX requirement and does not require a missing complementary capability elsewhere.
Changing estimate while draw not completed is consistent with other estimate-change and capture stories (PP-034, PP-033); complementary pieces present.

Displaying a thumbnail implies users must be able to provide/upload a photo or avatar; backlog contains account creation/change (PP-021, PP-023) but no explicit story to add/upload/manage a photo/avatar, exposing a missing complementary capability.
Standards compliance is a developer-level quality requirement and does not reveal a missing complementary functional capability in the backlog.
Providing definitions is standalone documentation work and does not require missing complementary functional capabilities elsewhere in the backlog.
Creating database indexes is a developer task supporting performance (PP-048) and not missing complementary functional requirements.
Browser compatibility requirements are non-functional constraints; they don't reveal missing complementary functional stories needed for a complete feature set.
Accessibility compliance is a quality goal and does not indicate a missing functional complement across the backlog.
Performance responsiveness is covered by developer stories (PP-045) and does not require additional functional capabilities to be complete.
Unicode support is a cross-cutting technical requirement; no missing complementary functional story is required to claim this capability in backlog context.
Sensible URLs is a UX/navigation requirement and does not indicate missing complementary functional capabilities across the backlog.
Nice error pages are a UX requirement but do not reveal a missing functional complement in the backlog.

The requirement to store results non-identifiably conflicts with other backlog stories that explicitly collect identifiable data (account creation PP-021, joining by name PP-029); there is no complementary story describing anonymization/pseudonymization or opt-out to implement non-identifiable storage.
Request for usage metrics is a standalone need; complementary data collection/export stories exist (transcripts, storage) so no missing capability is evident.
